cases.title: Gomorrah opens
cases.story: Bomber Command used Window for the first time in combat during the opening raid. Foil strips confused German radar and disrupted control of the night defence. The following raids over Hamburg included separate American daylight operations.

extra.label: RAF Bomber Command · opening Hamburg raid
extra.note: Opening night only. This figure excludes later Gomorrah raids.

extra.label: Contemporary operational report · Hamburg
extra.note: The report describes 751 aircraft in six phases following Pathfinder marking. Its scope differs from the campaign chronology’s 791 dispatched. The difference remains open.

extra.label: No. 619 Squadron · Lancaster crew
extra.locator: Biographical account · first operation as captain
extra.note: Knilans captained a No. 619 Squadron Lancaster that night. The museum account identifies the squadron participation without a squadron total.

cases.title: Schweinfurt and Regensburg
cases.story: The Eighth Air Force targeted aircraft production and ball bearings in one operation. The Regensburg force continued to North Africa. A fog delay separated the Schweinfurt force from the first wave, allowing German fighters to land and rearm.

extra.label: US Eighth Air Force · both waves
extra.locator: Vol. II, ch. 20 · 17 August double mission
extra.note: B-17s in both waves. The official narrative gives the same combined loss but reverses the wing split shown in the group archives.

extra.label: 4th Bombardment Wing · Regensburg
extra.locator: 17 August · Eighth Air Force operations · Air Task Force 2
extra.note: Part of the combined US totals. North Africa was the planned destination after the raid.

extra.label: 1st Bombardment Wing · Schweinfurt
extra.locator: 17 August · Eighth Air Force operations · Air Task Force 1
extra.note: Part of the combined US totals. Schweinfurt is the other target; the map pin locates Regensburg.

cases.title: Black Thursday
cases.story: German fighters intercepted the B-17 formations after their short-range escort turned back. This case compares the final US headquarters tally with a museum’s account of the German records for that date.

extra.label: US Eighth Air Force · final headquarters tally
extra.note: The 17 comprise five crashed in England and twelve scrapped. Dispatch and departure figures depend on the source’s counting point.

extra.label: German fighters · published loss account
extra.locator: Black Thursday · German records as cited
extra.note: The museum lists destroyed, written off and damaged separately. The underlying fighter ledger is not reproduced on the page.

cases.title: Big Week opens
cases.story: Mission 226 sent three bomber forces against the German aircraft industry. ZG 26’s daily figure shows losses in the air and damage on the ground at Wunstorf.

cases.title: Schweinfurt by day and night
cases.story: The Eighth Air Force struck several targets by day, including Schweinfurt. RAF Bomber Command returned to Schweinfurt after dark. Near Holzminden, III./ZG 26 met escorted B-24s consistent with the Gotha force’s route.

cases.title: American daylight raid on Berlin
cases.story: Mission 250 brought B-17s and B-24s deep into Germany with long-range escort. A ZG 26 unit return records five losses; the German command sheet separately records losses across its entire area that day.

extra.label: Luftflotte Reich · daily loss return · 6 March 1944
extra.note: Whole command and calendar day. The return’s 69 is a separate population from the 69 Eighth Air Force bombers lost.

cases.title: Nuremberg night raid
cases.story: German night fighters caught the stream on the outward leg in moonlight. The RAF’s 795 dispatched is common across the accounts. The number that attacked and the loss tally vary with the source and category.

extra.label: British official history · alternate attacking count
extra.locator: Vol. I · The Strategic Air Offensive (30/31 March)
extra.note: Retain alongside the Appendix 10 target row (616 attacked). A denominator crosswalk is unavailable.

extra.label: Bomber Command Museum of Canada · raid losses
extra.locator: 30/31 March · outward leg and final tally
extra.note: The museum describes 82 losses on the outward leg. Its 95 lost is a separate tally from the Appendix’s 94 missing.

extra.label: No. 78 Squadron · Halifax LK797
extra.locator: Combat account of Pilot Officer Cyril Barton, 30/31 March
extra.note: The museum describes a night-fighter attack on LK797, which continued to Nuremberg before reaching England and crashing. No German formation attribution is made here.

cases.title: Opening strike against synthetic oil
cases.story: Mission 353 struck a set of synthetic-oil plants, including Leuna near Merseburg. The official narrative and mission chronology give different dispatch totals. Each is shown with its own population label.

extra.label: USAF official history · 15 combat wings
extra.locator: Vol. III, ch. 6 · The First Oil Attacks
extra.note: Official narrative force count. The operational chronology’s Mission 353 target listings total 886 dispatched. The source-level difference remains open.

cases.title: Munich and the 332d Fighter Group
cases.story: The 55th Bombardment Wing raided rail and airfield targets around Munich. A separate 459th Bomb Group formation lost two identifiable B-24s during the 332d Fighter Group’s escort window.

cases.title: Nordstern and Lancaster HK545
cases.story: No. 115 Squadron lists Lancaster HK545 as missing. A loss investigation associates it with an overnight claim by Ernst-Wilhelm Modrow, 1./NJG 1. The two sources describe different locations, leaving the attribution open.

cases.title: Misburg and Mission 425
cases.story: The Eighth Air Force sent several forces over northern and central Germany. The German command return covers a much wider territory than the Hanover oil targets and therefore supports a same-day comparison at command level.

extra.label: Mission 425 · escort coverage
extra.locator: 20 June · Eighth Air Force strategic operations · Mission 425
extra.note: The 44 escorts indexed in the archive cover a partial force and cannot be read as the mission-wide escort count.

cases.title: Leuna and the November interception
cases.story: Mission 698 included a large force against the Leuna synthetic-oil plant and separate refinery and rail targets. The 398th Bomb Group archive includes the original loss report for Campbell’s crew. The German daily return separates aircraft destroyed in air combat from losses on the ground and other causes.

extra.label: US Eighth Air Force · Mission 698
extra.note: Full mission across five forces and multiple targets. The 968 were dispatched fighters across several tasks.

extra.label: 398th Bomb Group · Campbell crew
extra.note: One documented B-17 loss from the Leuna operation, contained within the wider US losses.

extra.label: Luftflotte Reich · daily loss return · 2 November 1944
extra.locator: VII/143 · PDF p. 25 · 2 November · Total (all types)
extra.note: Whole command day. The air-combat, ground-bombing and missing columns are already included in the enemy-action total.

cases.title: Berlin and the February 1945 strike
cases.story: B-17s struck Berlin’s Tempelhof rail target while B-24s went to Magdeburg. Bundesarchiv records document the raid’s impact in Berlin and identify the air-district files for further investigation.

extra.label: US Eighth Air Force · Mission 817
extra.note: Entire mission, including the separate Magdeburg target and fighter tasks.

extra.label: Air Task Force 1 · Berlin
extra.note: 937 B-17s attacked the primary rail target. This force and its losses form part of Mission 817.
